examples.template:
{{name}}
{{address}}

OBJECTIVE
Administrative Assistant position with a small professional service firm requiring dependable secretarial support, orderly office systems, staff supervision, and accurate basic bookkeeping.

OFFICE SKILLS
- Typing 78 wpm; transcription from Dictaphone; proofreading client letters, proposals, and plan reports.
- IBM PC experience with WordPerfect 5.0, Lotus 1-2-3 worksheets, and client mailing lists.
- Alphabetic, numeric, and client-subject filing; appointment calendars; travel arrangements; multi-line telephone coverage.
- Check registers, accounts payable vouchers, bank deposits, petty cash, and monthly expense summaries.

EXPERIENCE
Beacon Benefits Administration, Boston, MA
Senior Secretary / Office Coordinator, 1986-1990
- Supported two pension consultants and the office manager in a five-person employee benefits practice.
- Prepared plan amendment letters, meeting agendas, client binders, and monthly status lists.
- Reorganized closed and active client files, reducing lost-file searches and improving retrieval for annual reviews.
- Trained and scheduled a receptionist/typist; reviewed outgoing correspondence for neatness and consistency.
- Posted vendor invoices, maintained postage and supply logs, reconciled petty cash, and prepared deposit slips.

Harbor Ledger Services, Cambridge, MA
Administrative Clerk, 1983-1986
- Typed financial statements, engagement letters, and billing sheets for bookkeeping clients.
- Maintained manual ledgers, matched invoices to checks, and filed payroll tax forms by due date.

EDUCATION
Shawmut Business Institute, Boston, MA
Certificate in Secretarial and Bookkeeping Procedures, 1983

REFERENCES
Available upon request.

variants.label: Strong fit
variants.prompt: Create a strong-fit applicant with directly relevant experience and skills for the advertised position. Describe concrete job-relevant responsibilities and qualifications. Use a concise format with brief bullet points, 110 to 150 words.
variants.template:
{{name}}
{{address}}
STATIONARY ENGINEER

QUALIFICATIONS
- Chicago Stationary Engineer License; experienced in hospital physical plant coverage, boiler room safety, and preventive maintenance.
- Operate and tend high-pressure steam boilers, pumps, compressors, vacuum systems, hot water heaters, and auxiliary equipment.
- Keep log readings, test water, blow down boilers, adjust firing controls, and report needed repairs promptly.

EXPERIENCE
Stationary Engineer, Northwest Community Medical Center, Chicago, 1966-1970
- Maintained steam, heat, sterilizer supply, and chilled water service for a multi-wing medical facility.
- Responded to night and weekend calls; coordinated repairs with plumbers, electricians, and outside service men.

Maintenance Engineer, Marquette Linen Service, Chicago, 1962-1966
- Serviced boilers, traps, valves, motors, belts, and condensate return equipment.

EDUCATION
Chicago Technical Trade School, Power Plant Operation course, 1961.
References available upon request.

STATIONARY ENGINEER

SUMMARY
- Licensed Chicago stationary engineer with strong background in continuous boiler plant operation for institutional buildings.
- Skilled with low and high pressure steam, feedwater pumps, oil and gas burners, air compressors, refrigeration auxiliaries, and emergency repairs.
- Careful record keeper; accustomed to shift work, safety inspections, and dependable service to occupied facilities.

WORK HISTORY
Plant Engineer, Lakeside Rest Home and Clinic, Chicago, 1965-1970
- Ran boiler room serving patient rooms, kitchen, laundry, and treatment areas; maintained steady steam and domestic hot water.

TRAINING
Midwest Institute of Mechanical Trades, Stationary Engineering certificate, 1960.
Chicago Stationary Engineer License held in good standing.

variants.label: More detail
variants.prompt: Create a strong-fit applicant with directly relevant experience and skills for the advertised position. Include an expanded work history with specific duties and evidence of the advertised qualifications. Use a more detailed format, 200 to 240 words.
variants.template:
{{name}}
{{address}}

POSITION SOUGHT
Stationary Engineer for hospital power plant and building service operations.

LICENSE
Chicago Stationary Engineer License, current. Experienced with city inspections, boiler-room logs, and safe shift turnover.

WORK HISTORY
Riverview General Hospital, Chicago
Stationary Engineer, 1964-1970
- Operate and maintain two low-pressure steam boilers serving patient rooms, kitchen, laundry, sterilizers, and heating coils.
- Keep hourly readings on steam pressure, feedwater temperature, fuel use, stack condition, and make-up water; report irregular conditions promptly.
- Perform boiler blowdown, water treatment tests, burner cleaning, pump packing, valve repairs, trap checks, and condensate return maintenance.
- Maintain air compressors, vacuum pumps, emergency generator, hot-water heaters, and ventilation fans used in hospital service.
- Assist pipefitters and electricians during shutdowns; tag equipment and observe safe lockout practices customary to the plant.

Northwest Carton Manufacturing Company, Chicago
Assistant Operating Engineer, 1958-1964
- Fired boilers for process steam and winter heat on rotating shifts.
- Serviced feed pumps, strainers, gauges, belts, bearings, and fuel-oil equipment.
- Helped prepare boilers for annual inspection and hydrostatic testing.

EDUCATION AND TRAINING
West Side Technical Institute, Boiler Operation and Power Plant Practice, 1958.
Apprentice instruction in steam fitting, pump repair, and basic electrical controls.

QUALIFICATIONS
Dependable shift man with hospital experience, careful record keeping, and sound knowledge of steam, heat, water, and mechanical service. Available for day, evening, or relief assignments.

{{name}}
{{address}}

OBJECTIVE
Licensed Stationary Engineer position with a Chicago hospital requiring reliable operation of boilers, heating equipment, and mechanical services.

LICENSE AND CERTIFICATES
Chicago Stationary Engineer License, current. Completed safety instruction covering boiler-room firing, pressure controls, and fire prevention procedures.

EMPLOYMENT
Lakeview Towers Hotel and Annex, Chicago
Watch Engineer, 1962-1970
- Held independent watch over boiler room supplying heat, hot water, laundry steam, and kitchen service for a large occupied building.
- Operated gas-fired and oil-fired boilers, adjusted burners, checked safety valves, tested low-water cutoffs, and maintained daily operating sheets.
- Repaired circulating pumps, condensate units, steam traps, pneumatic temperature controls, exhaust fans, and domestic hot-water tanks.
- Coordinated seasonal start-up and lay-up, boiler washouts, tube cleaning, and work with outside service mechanics.
- Responded to no-heat, no-hot-water, noise, leak, and equipment complaints while keeping service interruptions short.

Ashland Park Infirmary, Chicago
Maintenance Mechanic and Relief Engineer, 1957-1962
- Assisted licensed engineer in a small health-care facility power room.
- Serviced sterilizer lines, radiator valves, vacuum equipment, sump pumps, belts, motors, and refrigeration compressors.
- Kept stock of gaskets, packing, gauge glass, oil, and common fittings; cleaned plant area for inspection.

EDUCATION
Calumet Trade School, Chicago, courses in stationary engineering, blueprint reading, and elementary electricity, 1956-1957.

STRENGTHS
Strong fit for hospital plant work: steady under pressure, accustomed to occupied-building operations, preventive maintenance, clear logs, and cooperation with nursing, housekeeping, laundry, and dietary departments.

LICENSE
Chicago Stationary Engineer License, current. Experienced with city inspections, boiler-room logs, and safe shift turnover.

Stationary Engineer, 1964-1970

Dependable shift man with hospital experience, careful record keeping, and sound knowledge of steam, heat, water, and mechanical service. Available for day, evening, or relief assignments.

records.title: UNIX/NETWORK ADMINISTRATOR - Auburn University College of Veterinary Medicine is searching for a Unix/Network Administrator. The position involves Solaris, Linux, Web Service, NT, and e-mail administration. Work involves network configuration, administration, support and maintenance. Work will include, but is not limited to: network operating systems, distributed applications, network software, user administration, maintaining various network services such as ftp, mail, www, samba/nfs, etc. This person will also be responsible for network security for the CVM, and will support network applications of a complex nature. Additional responsibilities will include some database administration, Perl, Awk, and shell scripting, along with C programming. Entry into the applicant pool requires a Bachelor's degree, or Associate Degree and 2 years' relevant experience, or High School (or equivalent) and 4 years of relevant experience where the ability to function at the desired level has been proven. Other desired qualifications include experience with Solaris, Unix sendmail, TCP/IP, TCP wrappers, WWW administration, DNS, User management, NIS+, Perl and Shell Scripting, Majordomo, Windows, and PC's. The selected candidate will be placed in a Level II, III, or IV position commensurate with their education and experience. For more information, contact Leon Bowman leon@vetmed.auburn.edu 334-844-3713 or visit http://www.vetmed.auburn.edu/#jobs Interested parties should send letter and resume to: Tommy Waldrop Employment Specialist Langdon Hall Auburn University, AL 36849 Auburn University is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer. Women and minorities are encouraged to apply.
